name: Aztreonam
route_note: IV or IM injection; nebulised aztreonam lysine (Cayston) for cystic fibrosis. Also combined with avibactam (Emblaveo).

discovery.note: Monobactams were found in bacteria such as Chromobacterium violaceum; aztreonam is a fully synthetic monocyclic beta-lactam.

tagline: Monobactam for Gram-negatives, usable in most penicillin-allergic patients
summary: Aztreonam is a monocyclic beta-lactam (monobactam) active only against aerobic Gram-negative bacteria, including Pseudomonas aeruginosa. It shows little cross-reactivity with penicillin allergy (except with ceftazidime) and is stable to metallo-beta-lactamases, which has revived interest in combining it with avibactam.
mechanism: Aztreonam binds with high affinity to PBP3 of Gram-negative bacilli, inhibiting septum formation and producing long filamentous cells that eventually lyse. It has essentially no affinity for Gram-positive or anaerobic PBPs.

Metallo-beta-lactamases (NDM, VIM, IMP) do not hydrolyse aztreonam, but the serine ESBLs and AmpC enzymes that commonly accompany them do; avibactam blocks those serine enzymes, so aztreonam-avibactam is active against many MBL producers.
uses: Gram-negative infections (urinary, lower respiratory, intra-abdominal, septicaemia) in patients with severe beta-lactam allergy
Chronic Pseudomonas aeruginosa lung infection in cystic fibrosis (inhaled)

history.title: Monobactams described
history.detail: Squibb scientists report naturally occurring monobactams and synthesise aztreonam.

history.title: Inhaled aztreonam
history.detail: The FDA approves Cayston (Gilead) for cystic fibrosis patients with Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

history.title: EU approval of aztreonam-avibactam
history.detail: The European Commission authorises Emblaveo (Pfizer) for serious Gram-negative infections with limited options.

history.title: US approval of aztreonam-avibactam
history.detail: The FDA approves Emblaveo for complicated intra-abdominal infections.

serious: Anaphylaxis (cross-reactivity possible with ceftazidime, which shares an identical side chain)

facts: Aztreonam and ceftazidime share the same R1 side chain, so allergy to one may predict allergy to the other.
